properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, in the same breath as settling the page and explicitly flagged as thinking out loud: *"might even be fun to create/generate a small video explaining what reflow2 is for somebody new to it /brainstorm"*.

Nothing here is intent. It is his idea and it is recorded so it is not lost, not so it is claimed.

DISTINCT FROM the page decision on purpose: that one is SETTLED and covers what the page renders. This is an unsettled question about a different artefact, in a different medium, with a different failure mode. Folding it in would have made a decided node read as half-decided.

═══ ⭐ WHY IT IS BETTER THAN "A NICE EXTRA", AND WORTH KEEPING EVEN IF DECLINED ═══

It plausibly answers the cost he accepted one sentence earlier. `dec:idea-what-is-on-reflow2s-public-page` rules that the page carries ONLY renderings, which means **it cannot carry a hand-written "here is what reflow2 is"** — so a newcomer meets a systems-engineering view before knowing what they are looking at. **An explainer is the orientation the ruling removed.** That is not why he suggested it, and the connection is recorded as an observation rather than attributed to him.

═══ ⚠️ THE TENSION, RECORDED BESIDE THE IDEA RATHER THAN AGAINST IT ═══

**A video is the least renderable artefact there is.** The page's whole claim is that its contents come out of the graph and are periodically refreshed. A video is hand-made, expensive to remake, and therefore **the one thing on that page guaranteed to go stale** — and it would sit there asserting, by adjacency, the same provenance as the renderings around it. That is the exact failure `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` was opened about, in the medium where it is hardest to fix.

⇒ Not an argument against it. An argument that **if it ships, it must be visibly a different KIND of thing from the renderings** — or the renderings' credibility pays for it.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **A HAND-MADE VIDEO.** Best quality, highest staleness cost, remade by hand every time reflow2 moves.
(b) **A GENERATED WALKTHROUGH DRIVEN BY THE GRAPH** — a scripted tour whose narration and visuals are projected from the same source as the views, so it re-renders with them. Closest to the page's own doctrine; unclear that the tooling exists.
(c) **NOT A VIDEO — AN ANIMATED OR INTERACTIVE RENDERING.** The loop, drawn from the graph and stepped through. `docs/loop-dag.html` already exists as a rendered page and is the nearest thing to a starting point. Keeps the only-renderings rule intact.
(d) **NOTHING, AND LET THE CONFESSIONS DO THE TALKING.** The page's honesty is the pitch; a newcomer who does not get it was not the audience. Cheapest, and consistent — at the cost of the orientation gap being real.

📌 NOT ASSESSED: whether anything in reach can actually generate (b). Nothing in reflow2 renders video, and no attempt was made to find out — recording the idea is not the same as scoping it.

⇒ SEQUENCED AFTER THE RELEASE, like the page. Nothing here is started.
properties.name: OPEN — a short generated video explaining reflow2 to someone new, and the tension that it is the one thing on the page that cannot be rendered from the graph
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill because he marked it as one. The skill's rule is followed exactly: the idea is not argued down, and the objection — that a video is the one artefact on that page which cannot be re-rendered — is recorded BESIDE it as an option-shaping constraint rather than used to dismiss it. An idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning; recorded with its objection, it keeps both.

Split from the page decision rather than appended to it, per the skill's rule that several unrelated questions mean several Decisions — and because that one is now settled, so anything unsettled living inside it would make a ruling look tentative.

The connection to the orientation gap is the one thing here he did not say. It is attributed as an observation, not to him, so a later reader can tell his idea from the reason it might matter.
